messages.subject: E4tools export format for GGIR
parts:
Hi everyone,

Thank you for all your hard work on this fantastic package!

I've been trying to get my empatica E4 data to work with the package. I used the E4tools GGIR export function and have that file saved as a csv. I have imported the csv and hope to configure it for use with GGIR using read.myacc.csv() and I'm running into some issues.
Specifically that the exported CSV from E4tools has one column (reference attached), but from my understanding, the input parameters into read.myacc.csv() require column numbers eg.`rmc.header.length` - Vector with three column (numbers) in which the acceleration signals are stored.

Are there any example files that show the desired format for the imported csv? Should I be separating the column values using the space and creating a wider dataframe? Did I miss a step in exporting the file in E4 tools and my current format is wrong? Any insight would be really appreciated.

Thanks so much in advance,
Nava

I have not worked with this for quite a while. Did you check the google groups conversation history? I vaguely remember that there have been a couple of conversations around this.

Also, you could try to reach out to Evan Kleiman who was involved in testing the GGIR functionality for E4 data when I implemented it: https://psych.rutgers.edu/research-opportunities/undergraduate-research-labs/1048-kleiman-evan.

If you want me to dive into this then I am happy to do so in the form of a paid consultancy as I think it would be good that if we get this clarified we immediately work on improving the GGIR documentation about this.

Best regards,

Vincent

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] E4tools export format for GGIR
parts:
Hi Nava,

You see one column because your csv-file viewer does not know how the columns are separated, e.g. tabs or comma.

GGIR expects comma separated files, so if the columns are not comma separate you may need to first convert the file such that columns are separated by a comma.

While experimenting with this first try to use GGIR function read.myacc.csv to read a segment of the file.

Another approach would be to enhance GGIR to be able to handle multiple types of column separators, e.g. tabs, comma.

Best, Vincent
